overview.system_goal: The system aims to simulate classroom interactions to understand the factors influencing teacher attention allocation among students, focusing on communicative expression versus socioeconomic or academic background.
overview.agent_types: The simulation includes Teacher Agents responsible for allocating attention and Student Agents with varied levels of expressive skills, academic performance, and socioeconomic status.
overview.environment_description: The environment represents a classroom setting where Teacher Agents pose questions, and Student Agents respond with verbal and non-verbal cues. The environment captures interactions influenced by personal and socio-academic factors.
overview.agent_interaction_focus: The primary focus is on Teacher Agents' decision-making process in selecting Student Agents to answer questions, based on their communicative expression, socioeconomic, and academic background.

design_concepts.interaction_patterns: Teacher Agents interact with Student Agents by asking questions and evaluating their responses based on expressive behavior and background characteristics.
design_concepts.communication_protocols: Communication occurs through verbal questions from Teacher Agents and verbal and non-verbal responses from Student Agents, influenced by predefined decision logics.
design_concepts.decision_mechanisms: Teacher Agents use a combination of thresholds for communicative expression, socioeconomic influence, and a dynamic weighting model to make attention allocation decisions.
design_concepts.attention_distribution_measurement: Attention inequality is measured using simulated Gini coefficients, assessing the disparity in attention based on various student attributes.

details.agent_behaviors: Teacher Agents prioritize attention based on communicative expression and consider socioeconomic and academic backgrounds, while Student Agents exhibit expressive behaviors influenced by their profiles.
details.decision_algorithms: Three decision algorithms are used: a communication threshold model, a social influence model, and a dynamic hybrid model combining multiple student characteristics.
details.specific_constraints: Constraints include predefined thresholds for communication skill influence and a weighting system balancing expressive, academic, and socioeconomic factors.
details.simulation_parameters: Key parameters include communication threshold, social influence weight, and dynamic weight adjustments for communication, academic, and background attributes.

metrics.name: attention_gini_coefficient
metrics.description: Calculates the Gini coefficient of attention distribution to measure inequality. Range [0, 1]: 0 = perfect equality, 1 = perfect inequality. This is the core metric for analyzing whether teacher attention is distributed fairly or concentrates on certain students.
metrics.calculation_logic: Aggregate attention_distribution records from all TeacherAgents. Each record contains {selected_student_id, attention_value, ...}. Sum attention_value for each unique student_id. Sort the aggregated attention values and apply the Gini coefficient formula: G = (2 * sum(i * x_i)) / (n * sum(x_i)) - (n+1)/n. Returns time-series data showing how inequality evolves.

metrics.name: student_attention_summary
metrics.description: Summarizes attention received by each student, including total attention, selection count, and average attention per selection. Provides detailed breakdown for identifying which students receive more/less attention.
metrics.calculation_logic: Aggregate all attention_distribution records across TeacherAgents. For each unique selected_student_id, sum attention_value (total attention) and count occurrences (selection count). Calculate average attention per selection. Returns dictionary with labels (student IDs), total_attention, selection_count, and avg_attention_per_selection arrays.

metrics.name: hand_raising_effectiveness
metrics.description: Analyzes the relationship between hand-raising behavior and being selected. Compares selection rates for students who raised hands versus those who did not. Helps understand if teachers preferentially select hand-raisers or actively engage non-participants.
metrics.calculation_logic: Combine attention_distribution (teacher selections) and raise_hand_history (student behaviors). Count total students who raised hands vs. did not raise hands. Count how many from each group were selected. Calculate selection rates: raised_selected_rate = selected_raisers / total_raisers, not_raised_selected_rate = selected_non_raisers / total_non_raisers. Returns comparison statistics.

metrics.name: question_difficulty_impact
metrics.description: Analyzes how question difficulty affects teacher selection patterns. Shows whether teachers select more/fewer students for questions of different difficulty levels. Helps understand if attention distribution strategies vary by task complexity.
metrics.calculation_logic: Extract difficulty and total_selected from each attention_distribution record. Group records by difficulty level (discretized to 0.1 precision). For each difficulty level, calculate average number of students selected per round. Returns arrays: difficulty_levels, avg_students_per_round, and total_rounds for each difficulty.

agent_types.TeacherAgent: Responsible for allocating attention among students based on their communicative expression, socioeconomic status, and academic performance, simulating how educators make decisions in a classroom setting.
agent_types.StudentAgent: Exhibits varied levels of expressive skills and characteristics such as socioeconomic status and academic performance, influencing how they are perceived and selected for interactions by Teacher Agents in the simulation.
